title: Muntahā al-isnād: where the chain ends

scenes.question: Where does the chain end?
scenes.summary: Three chains side by side end at the Prophet ﷺ, a Companion and a Successor, each holding its text card; a bracket names the last two athar.

scenes.question: Is it from the Prophet ﷺ?
scenes.summary: A table of sayings, acts and approvals, said outright or implied, beside the set phrases that count as raised, with a view for those who doubt two of them.

scenes.question: Who met whom?
scenes.summary: The Companion's and the Successor's definitions as paths of gates, how Companionship is known, and the mukhaḍram standing between two eras.

scenes.question: Does it look connected?
scenes.summary: Five chains with verdicts show what is and isn't musnad for Ibn Ḥajar, al-Khaṭīb and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr.

questions.question: Should implied marfūʿ keep its own scene, though it has a single term?
questions.context: §5.40 sets out sayings, acts and approval, each outright or implied, and a list of set phrases. It is the longest paragraph of the division but defines one term, marfūʿ ḥukman.

options.label: Own scene
options.description: Keep 'Is it from the Prophet ﷺ?' as a two-cell scene: the 2 × 3 table and the column of set phrases.

questions.question: How should the apostate the translation calls ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh be named?
questions.context: §5.41 names ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh and Ibn Khaṭal as men who met the Prophet ﷺ believing, left Islam and died out of it. The one usually named is ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh. A translation query.

options.label: Ibn Khaṭal only
options.description: Name only Ibn Khaṭal until the owner checks the Arabic.

options.label: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh and Ibn Khaṭal
options.description: Correct the name to ʿUbayd Allāh, if the owner confirms the Arabic reads so.

questions.question: Is 'Some: among the Companions' a fair Other view for the mukhaḍram?
questions.context: §5.42 says the matter is disputed. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr seemed to count them as Companions, and ʿIyāḍ and others said he did so outright; Ibn Ḥajar doubts that he meant it.

options.label: Keep the view
options.description: The switch slides the mukhaḍram figure from the Successors' row up to the Companions', with a dashed tag naming ʿIyāḍ's reading of Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr.

options.description: Show Ibn Ḥajar's placement only, and tell the dispute in the mukhaḍram note.

questions.question: How should the Successor's third rejected condition be named?
questions.context: §5.42 rejects adding long company, a sound hearing, and 'the condition of acknowledgement' to the Successor's definition. The last is possibly tamyīz, discernment.

options.label: 'or a further condition'
options.description: Two crossed chips (long company, a sound hearing) and the words 'or a further condition'.

questions.question: Should the 'not raised' view cover both disputed phrases?
questions.context: §5.40 reports dissent on 'from the sunna is…' (al-Ṣayrafī, Abū Bakr al-Rāzī, Ibn Ḥazm) and says the dispute is the same for 'we were ordered…', which a group disputes.

options.label: One view, both phrases
options.description: 'Some: not raised' marks both cards with a dashed 'could be someone else's' tag.
options.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 160 90" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><rect x="10" y="15" width="90" height="18"/><rect x="10" y="45" width="90" height="18"/><rect x="108" y="18" width="44" height="12" rx="6" stroke-dasharray="3 2"/><rect x="108" y="48" width="44" height="12" rx="6" stroke-dasharray="3 2"/></svg>

options.label: First phrase only
options.description: The view marks only 'from the sunna is…'; the order phrase's dissent goes into the note.
options.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 160 90" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><rect x="10" y="15" width="90" height="18"/><rect x="10" y="45" width="90" height="18"/><rect x="108" y="18" width="44" height="12" rx="6" stroke-dasharray="3 2"/></svg>

questions.question: May the phrase forms of §5.40 be quoted?
questions.context: The cards show forms the translation names as forms, in its English: 'from the sunna is…', 'we were ordered…', 'we used to…', 'I heard him say…'. The worked examples (ʿAmmār, Jābir, Abū Qilāba) are paraphrased without quotation marks.

options.label: Quote the forms, paraphrase the examples
options.description: A few words each, within the 'short fragments' rule.

options.label: Paraphrase everything
options.description: No quotation marks on any card, for example 'he says it is from the sunna'.

questions.question: Should the marfūʿ chain show a gap?
questions.context: §5.43: marfūʿ holds whether the chain is connected or not. A ghost in column 1 says so in the picture, but puts a break in the first chain a reader sees.

options.label: Show a ghost
options.description: Column 1 has a blinking ghost and a skip arrow, labelled 'raised, whether its chain is connected or not'.

options.description: Every chain is whole; the point is made by a label only.

questions.question: Add a link from 'Did he hear it from him?' to the mukhaḍram?
questions.context: The hidden scene's panel 3 draws two mukhaḍramūn. An XLink there to companions#mukhadram would join the two scenes, but changes a built al-Mardūd scene.

options.label: Add later
options.description: Leave al-Mardūd untouched on this branch; add the link in a follow-up once this division merges.

options.label: Add now
options.description: One XLink line under panel 3's names: 'mukhaḍram → Who met whom?'.

questions.question: Approve the dashed gold 'implied' arrow?
questions.context: Implied marfūʿ needs a link to the Prophet ﷺ that is neither narration (a solid flowing arrow) nor a gap (red dashed).

options.label: Dashed gold arrow
options.description: Gold, like the Companion's link to him, but dashed: counted as his, not said outright.

questions.question: Use any of the proposed annotations?
questions.context: p.312 (the Companions' fatwās and a saying of Mālik as examples), p.313 (athar is the same as ḥadīth for the majority), p.314 (musnad also names a collection ordered by Companion). None is in the translation's §5.40–5.44.

options.label: None for now
options.description: Keep them as proposals in notes/annotation-usage.md.

options.label: Use p.314
options.description: Add a Read as text extra on 'Does it look connected?' about musnad as a kind of book.

questions.question: Rule on the seven translation slips (design §9).
questions.context: Notably §5.41 ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh (q2), §5.42 'acknowledgement' (q4) and §5.44's bracket, which contradicts the line before.

options.label: Neutral wording until a ruling
options.description: The site avoids each disputed word, as the design lists.

options.label: Follow the translation
options.description: Use the translation's words where the owner confirms them.
